brand_names: Investigational - No approved brand name yet
drug_class: Antiretroviral combination — Non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) + Nucleoside reverse transcriptase translocation inhibitor (NRTTI)
purpose: This combination medication is being studied to treat HIV-1 infection in adults. It is designed to help keep the amount of HIV virus in your blood very low, which helps protect your immune system. Keeping the virus under control helps you stay healthier and reduces the risk of passing HIV to others.
how_it_works: HIV needs special tools called enzymes to make copies of itself inside your body. Doravirine blocks one of those tools called reverse transcriptase, stopping the virus from copying its genetic material. Islatravir works in a similar but slightly different way — it gets inserted into the virus copying process and causes it to stop, giving you two different lines of defense against the virus at once.
common_side_effects: Some people may notice headache, dizziness, tiredness, nausea, diarrhea, or difficulty sleeping. Some people have also reported feeling down or having changes in mood. These effects are often mild and may improve over time.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor, as the virus can become harder to treat. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some drugs can interact with this combination. Islatravir has been associated with a decrease in CD4 cells (immune cells) in some studies, so your doctor will monitor your blood counts closely. Tell your doctor if you feel depressed or have any mental health changes.
typical_dosing: As this combination is still being studied in clinical trials, the final approved dosing has not been established yet. In studies, it has generally been taken once daily by mouth. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
